thread:
kai: quick sync. i built a small fuzz harness to exercise eviction+prefetch+handoff races. called it 'prefetch-oracle' :) ran a few sims and found a flaky window where a canceled prefetch still left stale cache pages and triggered rehydrate storms.

rana: nice. what's the model of fuzzing? random ops or guided?

kai: hybrid. we replay real traces but inject randomized failure-injection tokens: prefetch-cancel, demote-force, owner-crash, network-delay. the harness also fuzzes timing of the demote_signalled write vs token transfer.

mike: can you paste the core harness loop?

kai: ```
for trace_event in trace {
  apply_event(trace_event)
  if rand() < fault_prob { inject(random_fault()) }
  drain_all_messages()
  validate_invariants()
}
```

jun: what invariants are we checking?

kai: top invariants:
- no read should observe kv that wasn't acknowledged by owner (RAwrite)
- token ownership single-source: only one node reports owner for a prefix
- demote completion requires owner ack unless forced by ops with audit flag
- prefetches cannot cause demote to complete faster (i.e., prefetch is speculative)

rana: you mentioned stale pages after cancel. root cause guess?

kai: we saw two-step race: prefetch cancels -> prefetcher returns early but doesn't clean its ephemeral buffers because it failed mid-flush; later another node sees low residency and triggers rehydrate -> double writes. fix is to guarantee cancel triggers cleanup callback that runs under same reservation guard used by prefetch start.

mike: is that a refactor or a shim?

kai: shim first: add prefetch_cancel_postcleanup(prefix) that is best-effort idempotent. longer term: unify prefetch lifecycle with reservation tokens so cleanup is enforced by kernel.

jun: telemetry additions from fuzz runs?

kai: yes, new metrics: fuzz.prefetch.cancel_leak_count, fuzz.handoff.invariant_violations, fuzz.trace.coverage_pct, and prefetch.cleanup.latency_p90. these are surfaced in canary dashboards.

ops-bot: created canary ticket: https://internal.redwood/ops/canaries/prefetch-oracle-2026 (draft) :eyes:

rana: rollout/testing plan?

kai: plan:
1) run fuzz harness over 72h on staging with full production traces; collect violation histogram
2) enable harness in probe mode in prod for 6h (metrics only) to gather coverage info
3) run canary with prefetch_cancel_postcleanup enabled on 10% nodes, run fuzz harness concurrently for 24h
4) expand if invariant violations drop to zero for 3 consecutive canaries

mike: failure domains & safety valves?

kai: safety valves: feature flag to disable prefetch_cancel_postcleanup, ops endpoint to force-clean a prefix: POST $ADMIN/prefixes/{id}/prefetch/cleanup, and auto-rollback on fuzz.handoff.invariant_violations > 0 for 10m.

jun: tests?

kai: unit tests for cleanup idempotency, integration where we simulate owner crash mid-prefetch, and property tests that run 10k randomized sequences asserting the invariants.

rana: please add a short doc in RFC follow-up about the harness so teams can reuse it for other subsystems.

kai: will do. opening RFC WIP: https://go.redwood/rfc/prefetch-oracle (WIP) :rocket:

mike: thanks, this looks actionable. can you attach a short runbook snippet in the RFC? ops wants quick steps.

kai: added runbook to RFC and the canary ticket. pinging ops for review.

ops-bot: note: remember to add alert: fuzz.handoff.invariant_violations > 0 -> pager to eng-runtime on-call.
